title: Creation of a Knee Joint-on-a-Chip for Modeling Joint Diseases and Testing Drugs
protocol: Design osteochondral and miniJoint bioreactors using computer software.
Transfer the design to a 3D printer.
Print the bioreactor parts with photopolymer ink.
Rinse the printed parts three times with 15 mL of 95% ethanol.
Crosslink the printed pieces for 200 seconds in a flashlight polymerization device.
Add O-rings to inserts and lids.
Test if the assembled parts fit.
Add 17 g of gelatin Type B to 500 mL of distilled water.
Mix on a shaker for 30 min at 37 °C.
Add 13 mL of methacrylic anhydride and shake overnight at 37 °C.
Aliquot GelMA into individual dialysis bags (~60 mL per bag).
Place the dialysis bags in distilled water with a stir bar.
Change water multiple times daily and leave bags at 4 °C overnight for 7 days of dialysis.
Freeze the GelMA at -80 °C after dialysis.
Proceed to lyophilization by placing the frozen GelMA in a vacuum chamber.
Ensure GelMA is completely dried before removal from the lyophilizer.
Dissolve the GelMA in Hank's balanced salt solution (15% w/v).
Adjust pH to 7.4 with small amounts of NaOH if necessary.
Supplement the solution with 1x antibiotic-antimycotic and 0.15% LAP based on volume.
Store the 15% GelMA solution at -20 °C protected from light.
Place 3D-printed dual-flow bioreactor chambers, lids, and inserts into autoclave bags.
Autoclave the contents at 121 °C for 20 min with steam followed by dry heat.
Soak bioreactor chambers, lids, and inserts in 15 mL of sterile phosphate-buffered saline overnight inside the biological safety cabinet.
Allow soaked items to dry.
Flush out bone marrow from femoral neck and head using a solution during surgery.
Resuspend flushed bone marrow in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's Medium (DMEM).
Filter the suspension through a 40 µm strainer.
Centrifuge the filtered suspension at 300 x g for 5 min.
Remove supernatant from centrifuged sample.
Resuspend pellets using growth medium consisting of DMEM, 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS), and 1x antibiotic-antimycotic.
Place resuspended cells into tissue culture flasks.
Change the culture medium every 3 to 4 days.
Ensure cell confluence reaches 70% to 80% before proceeding further.
Incubate cells with trypsin-EDTA for 2-3 min to detach them.
Passage detached cells at a ratio of 1 million cells per T150 flask.
Expand cells up to passage 5 (P5).
Centrifuge suspended cells after trypsinization at 300 x g for 5 min.
Resuspend cells at 20 x 10^6 cells/mL in a 15% GelMA solution using a 1,000 µL pipette.
Turn off the light of the biological safety cabinet.
Press a sterile, dry silicone mold against a Petri dish with forceps.
Place one insert into each hole of the silicone mold with the hole side facing down.
Using a 200 μL pipette, add the cell suspension to fill up the insert (~50 µL per insert).
Illuminate the top of the gel/insert for 1.5 min with UV light (wavelength 395 nm).
Illuminate the other side of the gel/insert for 30 s with UV light.
Transfer the inserts into 8 mL of growth medium in a non-tissue culture 6-well plate to allow the cells to recover overnight.
Differentiate the cells toward four lineages by transferring the inserts to 8 mL of adipogenic medium in each well of a non-tissue culture well plate.
Culture the cells for 28 days, changing the medium every other day.
Place the inserts into dual-flow bioreactor chambers.
Cap the wells.
Infuse the osteogenic medium at a flow rate of 5 µL/min with 35 mL of OM.
Infuse the chondrogenic medium at a flow rate of 5 µL/min with 35 mL of CM.
Maintain cell differentiation for 28 days by performing biweekly medium changes.
Differentiate the MSCs in 2D culture over 21 days using fibrogenic medium (FM).
Change the medium every week during differentiation.
Detach the cells using 4 mL of trypsin.
Encapsulate the 3D gels within the inserts to obtain synovial-like fibrous tissue (SFT).
Autoclave the 3D miniJoint bioreactor chambers.
Connect silicone tubing to the miniJoint bioreacher barb at one end.
Attach Luer lock connectors to the other end of the silicone tubing.
Prepare AM, OM (without BMP7), and FMCM as mentioned in step 2.11.
Create common shared medium (SM) using phenol red-free DMEM.
Add antibiotic-antimycotic solution to SM.
Include Na-pyruvate in SM.
Mix ITS into the SM.
Add 40 µg/mL proline to SM.
Include 50 µg/mL ascorbic acid in SM.
Add 0.5 ng/mL transforming growth factor β3 to SM.
Load 35 mL of each medium into reservoirs.
Transfer osteochondral unit from dual-flow bioreactor to right well of miniJoint bioreactor using straight forceps.
Insert adipose tissue into left well of miniJoint bioreactor.
Place fibrous tissue insert in the middle well of miniJoint bioreactor.
Cap all wells with sterilized lids.
Connect inlets of miniJoint chip to medium reservoirs.
Attach outlets of miniJoint chip to syringes.
Mount syringes onto a syringe pump.
Transfer pump and chips into an incubator.
Keep medium reservoirs on ice outside the incubator.
Operate pump in withdraw mode to draw medium from reservoirs into bioreactor chambers.
Add interleukin 1β (IL-1β) to the fibrogenic medium at a concentration of 10 ng/mL.
Replace syringes on the third day of IL-1β treatment.
Provide fresh IL-1β to the fibrogenic medium every three days for seven days total.
Administer the drug in the shared medium after three days of IL-1β treatment to simulate "intraarticular administration".
Alternatively, administer the drug in all media types after three days of IL-1β treatment to simulate "systemic administration".
Collect individual tissues for analysis after seven days of IL-1β treatment.
Use sterile curved forceps to remove the inserts.
Push a biopsy punch through the center of the insert to remove the gel.
Place the removed gel in PBS.
Cut the osteochondral gels in half for gene expression assessment.
Collect around 1.5 mL from each medium source.
Centrifuge the conditioned media at 14,000 x g for 10 min.
Discard the sediment after centrifuging.
Flash-freeze the conditioned media in liquid nitrogen.
Fix the OC and SFT samples in 10% buffered formalin.
Dehydrate the fixed samples in ethanol of ascending concentrations.
Clear the dehydrated samples in xylene.
Embed the cleared samples in paraffin.
Section the embedded samples at a thickness of 6 µm.
Fix the AT microtissues in 10% buffered formalin.
Directly stain the AT microtissue samples with Oil Red O solution or BODIPY.
